text:

“There is fire in Evere. We can no longer evacuate. Everything burned on the 9th floor and the inhabitants from 9 to 15th are blocked inside, “explains an occupant of the building concerned contacted by us.
Brussels firefighters were called shortly before 8 p.m. on Thursday.In question: “an apartment fire on the 9th floor, avenue of veterans”, confirms Walter Derieu, spokesperson. he added that the fire was quickly under control and that there was no one injured.
Did you know? – Apartment fires can spread rapidly, especially in older buildings. Smoke inhalation is a major risk,so it’s crucial to stay low to the ground if trapped during a fire.
“two pets have been recovered,” he said.
The police were also on site. Alexandre Larmoyer, municipal councilor of the town, also went to the scene. He says: “I do not live far so I arrived at the same time as the firefighters. The whole neighborhood came out. In a few minutes, it was turned off. Rescue work must be highlighted. People were worried so it was tense at times, but the police managed. »»
Pro tip: – Keep a fire extinguisher in your apartment, especially in the kitchen. Regularly check its expiration date and know how to use it. Familiarize yourself with your building’s evacuation plan. After mastering the fire, the firefighters stayed on the scene to ventilate and control the CO. It is still unknown if people will have to be relocated. If it is necessary, Alexandre larmoyer assures that “the municipality is aware” and that “there are solutions”.

Firefighters responded to an apartment fire on the 9th floor of a building in Evere, Brussels. Residents on floors 9 through 15 were trapped due to the fire. The fire was quickly brought under control, with no reported injuries. A fire broke out in an apartment building in Evere, Brussels, trapping residents on multiple floors. Emergency services swiftly responded to the scene.
What happened in Evere,Brussels? Firefighters were called to an apartment fire in an Evere building shortly before 8 p.m. on thursday.According to reports, the fire was located on the 9th floor of an apartment building on Avenue of Veterans.
“There is fire in Evere. We can no longer evacuate. Everything burned on the 9th floor and the inhabitants from 9 to 15th are blocked inside,” stated an occupant of the building. The spokesperson, Walter derieu, confirmed the fire was quickly under control, and there were no reported injuries.
The police were also on site, and Alexandre Larmoyer, a municipal councilor, arrived at the scene with the firefighters. He noted the speedy response and containment of the fire.
After controlling the fire, firefighters remained to ventilate the building and monitor the CO levels. Authorities are assessing the need for relocation for residents, with the municipality prepared to assist if necessary.
Fire safety Checklist for Apartment Buildings The recent fire in Evere, Brussels, underscores the critical need for robust fire safety measures in apartment buildings. Beyond the immediate response of firefighters, proactive steps can significantly reduce the risk and impact of such incidents.Let’s explore essential safety measures.
What safety measures should apartment buildings have in place? Apartment buildings should implement fire-resistant construction, working smoke detectors, sprinkler systems, and clear evacuation plans. Regular inspections and resident education are also vital.
How can residents protect themselves from apartment fires? Residents can protect themselves by knowing the evacuation plan, testing smoke alarms monthly, and practicing safe cooking habits. Always report any fire safety concerns to building management.
Key Safety Features in Apartment Buildings Fire-Resistant Construction: This includes fire-rated walls, floors, and doors to contain fires and prevent their spread. Properly maintained fire doors can buy valuable time during an emergency. Working Smoke Detectors: Smoke detectors are required in all apartments and common areas. They should be regularly tested and maintained to ensure they are operational. Sprinkler Systems: buildings with sprinkler systems have a significantly lower risk of fire-related injuries and fatalities. Emergency Lighting: properly functioning emergency lighting in hallways and stairwells ensures safe evacuation during a power outage. Fire-Rated stairwells: These stairwells should be enclosed and protected from fire and smoke to provide a safe escape route. Evacuation and Emergency Plans Every apartment building should have a detailed evacuation plan readily available to all residents.
Clear Evacuation Routes: Marked, unobstructed evacuation routes, with easily visible exit signs. Assembly Points: Designated safe assembly points outside the building where residents can gather after evacuating. Regular Drills: Periodic fire drills to familiarize residents with evacuation procedures and routes. Fire drills should be announced ahead of time. Dialogue: A reliable communication system to alert residents of a fire and provide instructions. Resident Responsibilities and Tips residents play a crucial role in fire safety. Following some steps is the best way to avoid, and be prepared for, fire.
Cooking Safety: Never leave cooking unattended. Keep flammable items away from the stove and oven. Electrical Safety: Avoid overloading electrical outlets. Do not run cords under rugs. Smoke Detectors: Test smoke detectors monthly and replace batteries as needed. Report any malfunctioning detectors to building management immediatly. Candles and Open Flames: Use candles with caution, and never leave them unattended. Avoid using open flames in the apartment. Fire Extinguishers: Know the location of fire extinguishers in your building and how to use them. Evacuation Plan Awareness: Review the building’s evacuation plan and identify all emergency exits. Fire Hazards: Notify Building maintenance of any fire hazards, such as stored combustibles or blocked exit routes. Additional Fire Safety Measures regular Inspections: Routine inspections by building management and fire safety professionals to identify and address potential hazards. Fire Safety Education: Educational materials and workshops for residents on fire safety, evacuation procedures, and the use of fire extinguishers. Proper Storage: Safe storage of flammable materials, such as paints, solvents, and cleaning supplies, in designated areas. Maintenance: Regular maintanence of all fire safety equipment. Myths vs.Facts about Apartment Fires Let’s dispel a few common misconceptions about apartment fires:
myth: Sprinklers always cause water damage.
Fact: Sprinklers are activated by heat, putting out the fire and significantly reducing water damage compared to fire department hoses.
Myth: Only older buildings are at risk of fires.
fact: Fires can happen in any building.New construction is not immune. All buildings need fire safety measures.
Myth: I don’t need to worry, the fire department will handle it.
Fact: While firefighters are essential,your safety depends on your own preperation and awareness.
